context: The domain of a function is the set of input values for which the function is defined. It is the set of all x-values for which the function is a valid mathematical expression.
The range of a function is the set of output values that the function can produce. It is the set of all y-values that the function can take.

concept_name: Domain and Range of a Function
context: When finding the domain and range of a function, we need to consider the values of x and y that make the function valid and the values that the function can produce.
A function can have an infinite domain if it is defined for all real numbers.
A function can have a finite domain if it is only defined for a specific set of values.
A function can have a finite range if it only produces a specific set of values.
A function can have an infinite range if it can produce all real numbers.
When finding the intersection of the domain and range of a function, we need to consider the values that the function is defined for and the values it produces.
When finding the union of the domain and range of a function, we need to consider the values that the function is defined for and the values it produces.
When finding the difference of the domain and range of a function, we need to consider the values that the function is defined for and the values it produces.
When finding the complement of the domain and range of a function, we need to consider the values that the function is not defined for and the values it does not produce.
